title: Lucentix pilot pre-decision econ readout
summary: Redwood and Lucentix reviewed week-5 pilot metrics, tuned batching/kv-cache settings, and aligned on business-case numbers for exec sign-off. Customer requested final pricing, SOC2 + KMS notes, and a short exec readout next Tuesday. Agreed to run two final microbenchmarks (24h) and deliver ROI spreadsheet.

transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2025-12-17
Time: 15:00 PST
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Hayes (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Alex Chen (Redwood CSM), Marta Ruiz (Head of Data, Lucentix), Samir Patel (CTO), Ellie Wong (Procurement), Diego Alvarez (Product Lead)

Summary (auto): Quick econ readout, validate success criteria, finalize commercial ask, security gating review.

[00:00] Jordan Hayes: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick roll call?
[00:06] Marta Ruiz: Marta here.
[00:08] Samir Patel: Samir on.
[00:10] Ellie Wong: Ellie, procurement.
[00:12] Diego Alvarez: Diego here.
[00:14] Priya Nair: Priya from Redwood.
[00:16] Jordan Hayes: Great. Alex?
[00:18] Alex Chen: Alex here.
[00:20] Jordan Hayes: Cool, objective for today is run through the week-5 pilot numbers, confirm tuning changes we made midweek, and align the business case so you can take to your execs. We'll also call out any security docs you still need.

[02:05] Priya Nair: I'll start with the perf highlights — we moved from the hosted-default batching to a ded-1 profile with tighter concurrency, and enabled prefix/KV cache for the top 12k tokens. That dropped average 95p latency from ~280ms to about 170ms on the core flow. Throughput stayed around 380 r/s sustained during the 3-hour window we probed. There was a small uptick in cold-start p95 when caches were flushed, so we recommend a warm-up window for steady-state.

[03:20] Diego Alvarez: Sorry, can you repeat the 95p numbers? I think I heard 170 but earlier notes said 220.
[03:26] Priya Nair: Yeah, good catch. Default run earlier in the week was 280ms p95, after the ded-1 config + cache we consistently saw 160-180ms p95 across the workload slices we care about. The 220 was from one noisy snapshot where a node had a transient I/O.

[04:40] Marta Ruiz: And cost? We need the delta to our baseline.
[04:45] Jordan Hayes: Right, so in the pilot we tracked token-cost plus instance amortization. Per 1,000 end-user queries the incremental cost using ded-1 was roughly $0.42 — that's a ~28% reduction vs the initial hosted run where we measured $0.59 per 1k. Those are pilot-level numbers; final committed pricing would change with reserved capacity.

[06:10] Samir Patel: That reduction looks good. What's the conservative projection for committed reserved capacity? If we go dedicated, what's the unit cost change?
[06:18] Jordan Hayes: For a reserved 3-month commit, thermalized and assuming steady throughput, we estimate a per-1k cost of $0.30 when factoring in burst/dedicated discounts. We'll put a full sliding scale in the spreadsheet.

[07:05] Ellie Wong: From procurement, we need to see the SOW, termination terms, and the SOC2/ISO notes. Also KMS integration story — we operate with a customer-managed KMS.

[07:20] Alex Chen: We'll attach SOC2 artifact and the KMS integration runbook. Redwood supports both cloud KMS and HSM via our private deployment; for Dedicated you can bring your key via KMIP/HSM or use provider KMS. We'll surface the recommended config.

[08:40] Diego Alvarez: On success criteria — we proposed three items: p95 latency <200ms for core flows, cost per 1k queries < $0.50, and accuracy/quality measured via the 200-sample eval set with regression <2% vs baseline. Are we aligned on that?

[09:02] Marta Ruiz: Those look right but can we tighten latency to <180ms? That's what the product team needs to sign the UX improvements.

[09:15] Priya Nair: Based on the runs today, <180ms p95 is achievable with the ded-1 profile plus prefix caching. Two caveats: 1) cold-cache drops can spike p95 briefly; 2) sequence length variance will affect tail latency. We mitigated some of that with token-bucketing.

[10:35] Samir Patel: What's the failure mode fallback if the dedicated pool is saturated? We need to avoid impact during peak.

[10:42] Jordan Hayes: Redwood's routing policy can failover to a compatible hosted variant with a slightly higher cost; there's also auto-burst capacity we can enable. For enterprise we can set an SLA-backed burst policy so critical traffic is never rejected — it just costs more during those windows. We can include a fallback policy in the SOW.

[12:00] Ellie Wong: On data residency — the pilot used regional us-west infra; our compliance team asked if logs can be redacted and if audit logs can be forwarded to our SIEM.

[12:12] Alex Chen: Yes — audit logs can be forwarded over syslog/S3 to your SIEM with role-based access. We also support log redaction hooks prior to export; we'll include the config snippet.

[13:50] Priya Nair: Quick note on quality: we ran the 200-sample eval set after the quantization tuning. The model showed a 0.9% drop in task-specific F1, which is within your 2% threshold. We also ran a manual spot-check for out-of-distribution prompts and flagged three edge cases where hallucination risk increased; we've included prompts in the shared doc for review.

[15:05] Diego Alvarez: Can you remind me which quantization profile you used? I want to reproduce it locally.

[15:12] Priya Nair: We used q4fa-compat with int8 cross-layer fallback on last-8 layers. It's in the config link Jordan will send. The tradeoff there is small accuracy delta for big perf gains.

[16:40] Marta Ruiz: From the business case perspective, if we get to the <180ms p95 and cost <= $0.40 per 1k with reserved pricing, the execs will likely greenlight an initial 6-month pilot with an option to expand. We need the final ROI slide to show break-even month and projected MTTR improvements for support agents.

[17:10] Jordan Hayes: Absolutely. We'll include a break-even chart in the spreadsheet. Alex, can you confirm the support MTTR assumptions we used?
[17:18] Alex Chen: We modeled a 22% reduction in average handle time based on the decreased latency and improved response relevance — translates to about $45k per quarter for the volumes you gave us. We'll annotate the assumptions so you can tweak them in the sheet.

[18:50] Samir Patel: A couple of technical deep-dive items before we finalize: 1) KV cache eviction policy, 2) how model rollouts are handled without impacting live traffic. Priya?
[18:58] Priya Nair: KV caches follow an LRU with a hot-prefix pinning option; for your workload the hot-prefix pin helped a lot. For rollouts we do canary first — small % to new model variant, monitor quality and latency, then ramp. If regressions occur we have automatic rollback to last known-good variant. We can pass the rollout playbook.

[21:20] Diego Alvarez: Is there any manual tuning left that you'll need from our side? Like prompt templates or tokenization changes?
[21:27] Priya Nair: We recommended two prompt template changes to reduce token count — small edits in the system prompt and truncation heuristics. We'll post diffs in the doc so your team can apply and test.

[23:05] Jordan Hayes: Procurement question — Ellie, aside from SOW and SOC2, anything else that blocks final sign-off?
[23:12] Ellie Wong: Need payment terms, SLAs, indemnity clause — standard stuff. Also a clause on data deletion post-contract. If Redwood can accept a 60-day termination with pro-rated refunds, that's cleaner for us.

[24:00] Jordan Hayes: We typically do 90-day notice for reserved contracts, but for pilots we can do 60-day. We'll mark that in the SOW draft.

[26:10] Marta Ruiz: Ok, decision gates — we want a short exec readout where Redwood presents the final numbers and the proposed commercial, then we expect a sign-off within 2 weeks if everything looks good. Can we target the week of 2025-12-22?

[26:28] Jordan Hayes: That works. We'll aim to deliver the pricing and security package Friday 12/19 so you have time to prep.

[28:00] Priya Nair: About the final benchmarks — I'll run a 24h microbenchmark overnight on the ded-1 config with prefix caching and token-bucketing enabled; that should surface tail behaviors. I'll share results and raw logs.

[29:45] Samir Patel: How reproducible are these runs? We might want to run the same bench on a staging cluster with our traffic pattern.

[29:52] Priya Nair: We'll provide the benchmark harness and a reproducible config — it's the same script we've used for the pilot plus a traffic sample. We can also help run a mirrored test if you grant access to staging.

[32:10] Diego Alvarez: One last UX question — any latency differences for streaming responses vs non-streaming? We have a use-case where early tokens are critical.

[32:18] Priya Nair: Streaming reduces perceived latency because tokens arrive earlier, but total end-to-end time can be similar. For your case we recommend streaming the first 3 tokens as soon as they are produced while still sustaining low p95 for the full response; that combination gave the best UX in our tests.

[34:00] Marta Ruiz: Alright, let's recap commitments.
[34:05] Jordan Hayes: Recap: Redwood — pricing & SOW (Jordan) by 12/20, security pack + SOC2 and KMS notes (Alex) by 12/19, 24h microbench + logs (Priya) by 12/19. Lucentix — schedule exec readout (Marta) by 12/18 and confirm attendees. Technical follow-ups: Priya will post prompt diffs and quant profiles.

[35:20] Ellie Wong: Quick procurement clar — can you email the SOW in PDF with change-tracking enabled so legal can comment inline?
[35:28] Jordan Hayes: Yes. We'll send tracked PDF and a clean copy.

[36:40] Diego Alvarez: A few transcribed notes — we saw three edge-case hallucination prompts; I want those in the shared doc.
[36:46] Priya Nair: Already uploaded — under Pilots/Alerts -> Hallucination-cases-1217.

[38:00] Alex Chen: I'll also add the MTTR spreadsheet and the break-even slide; you'll be able to toggle conservative/optimistic assumptions.

[40:10] Samir Patel: Any outstanding legal or export controls? We are fine with US-region but will need EU residency later — flagging it.

[40:22] Jordan Hayes: Noted. We support region pinning; we'll call out EU region availability and timeline in the doc.

[42:00] Marta Ruiz: If everything is in order, we should be able to have a decision within two weeks of the readout.

[42:10] Jordan Hayes: Great. Any final questions before we wrap?
[42:18] Ellie Wong: No, just the usual — confirm payment terms and termination language in SOW.
[42:25] Jordan Hayes: Will do.
[43:40] Priya Nair: One more quick technical note — during the ded-1 runs, the CPU on the orchestration node spiked briefly at 65% under heavy batching; we've opened an infra ticket to tune the batching scheduler but it's not blocking. We'll include the infra ticket link.
[44:02] Diego Alvarez: Ok thanks.
[45:00] Jordan Hayes: Thanks everyone. We'll follow up with the attachments. Expect the readout scheduling email from Marta to include possible time slots; Redwood will hold Tue/Wed mornings next week.
[45:18] Marta Ruiz: Sounds good.
[45:35] Samir Patel: Thanks all.
[45:40] Ellie Wong: Thanks, bye.
[46:00] Alex Chen: Thanks — bye.

End of transcript.

Shared links referenced: pilot-dashboard (internal), Pilots/Alerts/Hallucination-cases-1217, ROI-spreadsheet-draft, SOC2-summary.pdf, KMS-integration-runbook.pdf, SOW-draft-v2.pdf
